title: Genesis Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 31.

questions.question: Who heard the words of Laban's sons complaining about Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:1 states that Jacob heard the words of Laban's sons.

questions.question: How did Jacob perceive Laban's countenance compared to before?
options: It was not toward him as before
questions.correctAnswer: It was not toward him as before
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:2 says Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban and saw it was not as before.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give Jacob in Genesis 31?
options: Return to the land of thy fathers and kindred
questions.correctAnswer: Return to the land of thy fathers and kindred
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:3 records the LORD telling Jacob to return to his father's land and kindred.

questions.question: Whom did Jacob call to the field unto his flock?
questions.correctAnswer: Rachel and Leah
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:4 states Jacob called Rachel and Leah to the field.

questions.question: What did Jacob say about the countenance of Rachel and Leah's father?
options: It was not toward him as before
questions.correctAnswer: It was not toward him as before
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:5 shows Jacob telling Rachel and Leah he saw their father's countenance was not as before.

questions.question: How long did Jacob say he had served Laban with all his power?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty years
questions.explanation: Although the exact twenty years is mentioned later, here Jacob says 'with all my power I have served your father' indicating the long service explained fully in verse 38 with twenty years.

questions.question: How many times had Laban changed Jacob's wages?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten times
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:7 states Laban changed Jacob's wages ten times.

questions.question: What types of cattle did Laban say would be Jacob's wages?
questions.correctAnswer: Speckled and ringstraked
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:8 explains the wages were speckled or ringstraked cattle.

questions.question: According to Jacob, who took away Laban's cattle and gave them to him?
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:9 says God took away the cattle of Laban and gave them to Jacob.

questions.question: What did Jacob see in a dream when the cattle conceived?
options: The rams leaped upon the cattle and were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled
questions.correctAnswer: The rams leaped upon the cattle and were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:10 describes Jacob's dream of rams that were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled leaping upon the cattle.

questions.question: Who spoke to Jacob in a dream saying 'Jacob: And I said, Here am I'?
questions.correctAnswer: The angel of God
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:11 records the angel of God speaking to Jacob in a dream.

questions.question: True or False: Rachel and Leah asked Jacob if there was any inheritance for them in their father's house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:14 shows Rachel and Leah asking if any portion or inheritance remained for them.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob secretly fled from Laban without telling him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:20 states Jacob fled unawares to Laban, not telling him.

questions.question: True or False: Laban blessed his sons and daughters before departing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Blessing of sons and daughters by Laban before departing is recorded in Genesis 31:55, beyond the first third of the chapter, so not referenced for early verses here.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob set his sons and wives upon camels before leaving.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:17 says Jacob rose and set his sons and wives upon camels.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did Jacob leave Laban without his knowledge according to Genesis 31?
options: Jacob fled secretly without telling Laban
Jacob sent a message to Laban
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob fled secretly without telling Laban
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:20 states that Jacob stole away unawares to Laban and did not tell him that he fled, indicating he left secretly.

questions.question: What geographical feature did Jacob cross when he fled from Laban?
questions.correctAnswer: The river
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:21 describes Jacob passing over the river as he set his face toward Mount Gilead, indicating the river was crossed during his flight.

questions.question: How many days did Laban pursue Jacob before overtaking him?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:23 says Laban pursued Jacob for seven days' journey before overtaking him in Mount Gilead.

questions.question: What warning did God give Laban in a dream regarding Jacob?
options: Do not speak to Jacob either good or bad
Do not harm Jacob or his family
Bless Jacob and send him away safely
questions.correctAnswer: Do not speak to Jacob either good or bad
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:24 records God’s command to Laban in a dream to take heed not to speak to Jacob either good or bad, protecting Jacob from harm.

questions.question: What was Laban's initial accusation against Jacob upon overtaking him?
options: That Jacob stole away unawares and carried away his daughters like captives
That Jacob had stolen his cattle
That Jacob had lied about his wages
That Jacob had broken a covenant
questions.correctAnswer: That Jacob stole away unawares and carried away his daughters like captives
questions.explanation: In Genesis 31:26, Laban accuses Jacob of stealing away secretly and carrying away his daughters as if taken by force, highlighting Laban’s feeling of betrayal.

questions.question: Why did Jacob say he fled secretly from Laban?
options: He feared Laban would forcibly take his daughters from him
He wanted to take all the cattle quietly
He was angry at Laban's treatment
He received a direct command from God to flee
questions.correctAnswer: He feared Laban would forcibly take his daughters from him
questions.explanation: Jacob answered Laban in Genesis 31:31 that he fled because he feared Laban would take his daughters by force, showing his protective concern.

questions.question: Who had stolen Laban's household gods, unknown to Jacob?
questions.correctAnswer: Rachel
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:32-34 reveal that Rachel had stolen her father's images without Jacob's knowledge, hiding them in the camel’s furniture.

questions.question: How did Rachel hide the images from her father when he searched for them?
options: She sat on them and claimed she could not rise due to her monthly sickness
She buried them in the ground
She gave them to one of the maidservants
She hid them in Jacob's tent
questions.correctAnswer: She sat on them and claimed she could not rise due to her monthly sickness
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:34-35 describe Rachel sitting on the images and telling her father she could not rise because of the custom of women, preventing him from finding them.

questions.question: True or False: Jacob was angry and confronted Laban after he searched for the household gods.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:36 shows Jacob was wroth and chode with Laban, asking what trespass he had committed to be so hotly pursued.

questions.question: What did Jacob challenge Laban to do after being searched and accused unjustly?
options: Set before their brethren all his household stuff to judge
Return to his own home with blessings
questions.correctAnswer: Set before their brethren all his household stuff to judge
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:37 records Jacob asking Laban to set before their brethren all his household belongings so they may judge between them fairly.

questions.question: According to Jacob, how many years did he serve Laban, and how were those years divided?
options: Twenty years: fourteen for daughters and six for cattle
Ten years: five for daughters and five for cattle
Fifteen years: ten for daughters and five for cattle
Twenty-five years: twenty for daughters and five for cattle
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty years: fourteen for daughters and six for cattle
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:41 states Jacob served Laban twenty years, fourteen for his two daughters and six years for his cattle.

questions.question: How does Genesis 31 teach about trusting God during difficult labor and unfair treatment?
options: Jacob credits God for seeing his affliction and protecting him
Jacob takes revenge on Laban immediately
Jacob accepts his fate silently without complaint
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob credits God for seeing his affliction and protecting him
questions.explanation: In Genesis 31:42, Jacob acknowledges that God's presence preserved him despite Laban’s changing wages and affliction, demonstrating faith and trust in God during hardship.

questions.question: True or False: Laban agreed that Jacob’s daughters and children were his own and that all cattle and possessions belonged to Jacob after their dispute.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:43 shows Laban claiming the daughters, children, and cattle were his, emphasizing his ownership and dispute with Jacob over possessions.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the heap and pillar that Jacob and Laban set up between them?
options: A witness and covenant to not harm each other
A boundary marker for cattle grazing
questions.correctAnswer: A witness and covenant to not harm each other
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:44-52 describe the heap and pillar as a witness between Jacob and Laban, symbolizing their covenant not to harm one another or cross boundaries for harm.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD promised Jacob in this chapter that He would be with him if he returned to the land of his fathers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:3 records the LORD telling Jacob to return to his father's land and kindred, promising His presence with him.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 31.

questions.question: What reason did Jacob give for fearing Laban when he stole his gods?
options: He thought Laban would take his daughters by force
He planned to sell the idols
He wanted to curse Laban's household
questions.correctAnswer: He thought Laban would take his daughters by force
questions.explanation: Jacob said he was afraid because he thought Laban might take his daughters by force, so he stole the gods as a precaution (Genesis 31:31).

questions.question: How long did Jacob serve Laban in total, according to Jacob's speech?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty years
questions.explanation: Jacob states he served Laban twenty years in total: fourteen for his daughters and six for his cattle (Genesis 31:41).

questions.question: What did Jacob say about the losses he sustained from torn animals?
options: He bore the loss himself and did not require compensation
He demanded full payment for every loss
He blamed Laban for the losses
questions.correctAnswer: He bore the loss himself and did not require compensation
questions.explanation: Jacob explains that when animals were torn by beasts, he bore the loss himself and Laban required it from his hand whether stolen by day or night (Genesis 31:39).

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by the heap of stones and pillar that Jacob and Laban set up as a witness?
options: Inclusio, marking the boundary of their covenant
Simile, comparing their covenant to stones
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, marking the boundary of their covenant
questions.explanation: The heap and pillar act as an inclusio, marking the covenant boundary and serving as a physical witness between Jacob and Laban (Genesis 31:45-51).

questions.question: Which name did Laban give to the heap of stones they set up?
questions.correctAnswer: Jegarsahadutha
questions.explanation: Laban called the heap Jegarsahadutha, while Jacob called it Galeed (Genesis 31:47).

questions.question: What does the name 'Mizpah' signify in the covenant between Jacob and Laban?
options: The LORD watching between them when they are apart
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD watching between them when they are apart
questions.explanation: Mizpah signifies that the LORD watches between Jacob and Laban when they are absent from one another (Genesis 31:49).

questions.question: According to Jacob, what would have happened if the God of his father had not been with him?
options: Laban would have sent him away empty-handed
He would have been blessed with more cattle
He would have taken Laban's daughters by force
He would have stayed longer with Laban
questions.correctAnswer: Laban would have sent him away empty-handed
questions.explanation: Jacob says that except for the God of his father, he would have been sent away empty by Laban (Genesis 31:42).

questions.question: How did Laban respond to Jacob’s recounting of his service and hardships?
options: He acknowledged his daughters, children, and cattle as his own and proposed a covenant
He accused Jacob of stealing all his wealth
He demanded that Jacob return immediately
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledged his daughters, children, and cattle as his own and proposed a covenant
questions.explanation: Laban responded by affirming his ownership of his daughters, children, and cattle, and proposed making a covenant as a witness between them (Genesis 31:43-44).

questions.question: What ritual act did Jacob perform after making the covenant with Laban?
options: He offered a sacrifice upon the mount
He built an altar of cedar wood
He wrote the covenant on a scroll
questions.correctAnswer: He offered a sacrifice upon the mount
questions.explanation: After the covenant, Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mount and called his brethren to eat bread (Genesis 31:54).

questions.question: What cultural significance does the act of Laban kissing his sons and daughters before departing carry?
options: A customary gesture of blessing and farewell
A sign of anger or accusation
questions.correctAnswer: A customary gesture of blessing and farewell
questions.explanation: Laban kissing his children before departing was a customary gesture of blessing and farewell in the ancient Near Eastern culture (Genesis 31:55).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God watching over a covenant when parties are absent, similar to Genesis 31:49?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 121:4
questions.explanation: Psalm 121:4 speaks of the LORD watching over His people, echoing the theme in Genesis 31:49 where God watches between Jacob and Laban when they are apart.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'heap' in Genesis 31:46 is often associated with what kind of ancient Near Eastern practice?
options: A boundary marker or witness for covenants
questions.correctAnswer: A boundary marker or witness for covenants
questions.explanation: The 'heap' (Hebrew: gāmal) served as a boundary marker or witness in covenants in the ancient Near East, as seen in Genesis 31:46.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God's faithfulness and protection seen in Jacob's experience with Laban?
questions.correctAnswer: Hebrews 11:21
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:21 mentions Jacob's faith in God's promises, reflecting God's faithfulness and protection during his time with Laban (Genesis 31:42).

questions.question: True or False: Jacob changed Laban's wages ten times according to Genesis 31.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It was Laban who changed Jacob's wages ten times, not Jacob himself (Genesis 31:41).

questions.question: True or False: The covenant between Jacob and Laban included a mutual agreement to not harm each other or pass the heap and pillar to do harm.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The covenant included a witness heap and pillar with the agreement that neither would pass over it to harm the other (Genesis 31:51-52).

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's protection over Jacob despite Laban's deception regarding his wages?
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:7 shows that although Laban deceived Jacob and changed his wages ten times, God did not allow Laban to harm Jacob, demonstrating God's providential care.

questions.question: According to Genesis 31:3 and 31:13, what was God's command to Jacob and what does it reveal about God's covenant faithfulness?
options: To return to his homeland and family, with God's presence assured
To build a temple to God in Padanaram
To conquer the land of Canaan by force
questions.correctAnswer: To return to his homeland and family, with God's presence assured
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:3 and 31:13 reveal God commanding Jacob to return to his father's land and kindred, promising His presence, demonstrating God's faithfulness to His covenant promises to the patriarchs.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Jacob’s declaration that 'God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me'?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine Sovereignty in Blessing
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:9 shows that God sovereignly transferred wealth from Laban to Jacob, illustrating the doctrine that God controls and bestows blessings according to His will.

questions.question: How does the episode of Rachel stealing her father's images (teraphim) contribute to the narrative and theological understanding of idolatry in the patriarchal context?
options: It shows Rachel's faithfulness to God over her father’s idols
It reveals the patriarchal acceptance of idolatry
It is a sign of Rachel's future as a priestess
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Rachel's faithfulness to God over her father’s idols
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:19 and 31:34-35 reveal Rachel’s secret theft of her father’s images, which can be interpreted as a rejection of idolatry and loyalty to the God of Jacob, marking a contrast between the worship of God and idols.

questions.question: What does Jacob’s response to Laban’s pursuit (Genesis 31:36-42) teach about the doctrine of human labor under divine oversight?
options: Human effort is irrelevant without divine blessing
Labor is a curse from God
questions.correctAnswer: Human effort is irrelevant without divine blessing
questions.explanation: Jacob recounts his hard work and Laban’s unfair treatment but emphasizes God’s presence and blessing (Genesis 31:41-42), teaching that human labor is sustained and rewarded under divine providence.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine intervention in human affairs is merely superstition. What does Genesis 31:24-29 actually teach about God's active involvement in human conflicts?
options: God actively intervenes to restrain harm and direct outcomes
God is unaware of human disputes
God encourages conflict to test faith
questions.correctAnswer: God actively intervenes to restrain harm and direct outcomes
questions.explanation: In Genesis 31:24-29, God appears to Laban in a dream warning him not to harm Jacob, showing God's active role in protecting His covenant people and controlling the course of events.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly displayed in the dream where the angel reveals to Jacob that God has observed all of Laban’s actions towards him?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:11-12 reveal God's omniscience as He shows Jacob that He has seen all Laban has done, demonstrating God's all-knowing nature.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Genesis 31:5-6 and Genesis 31:11 convey about God's presence and guidance in the believer's life amidst adversity?
options: God's presence is assured and He guides through revelation despite challenges
Human wisdom is superior to divine guidance
Believers must rely solely on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence is assured and He guides through revelation despite challenges
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:5-6 shows Jacob recognizing God's presence amidst Laban's changed attitude, and Genesis 31:11 records God's angel speaking to him in a dream, affirming divine guidance through adversity.

questions.question: How does the covenant made between Jacob and Laban in Genesis 31:44-53 reflect on the biblical theology of covenant as a divine-human agreement?
options: It shows covenants are merely human contracts
It demonstrates covenants involve mutual witness and divine sanction
It negates the need for divine involvement
It is unrelated to God's covenant with Abraham
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates covenants involve mutual witness and divine sanction
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:44-53 includes the setting of a heap and pillar as witnesses and invokes God as judge, illustrating the covenant as a solemn agreement witnessed by both parties and God.

questions.question: What theological insight does Genesis 31:42 provide regarding God's justice and care for the oppressed?
options: God sees affliction and works to rebuke oppressors
questions.correctAnswer: God sees affliction and works to rebuke oppressors
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:42 expresses Jacob's confidence that God has seen his affliction and labor and has rebuked Laban, showing God's justice and care for the oppressed.

questions.question: In light of Genesis 31:17-18, how does this chapter contribute to the redemptive narrative concerning obedience to God's call and the theme of pilgrimage?
options: It exemplifies faithful obedience by leaving to return to God's promises
It promotes settling permanently in foreign lands
It denies God's promises to the patriarchs
questions.correctAnswer: It exemplifies faithful obedience by leaving to return to God's promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:17-18 narrates Jacob rising to leave with his family and possessions to return to Canaan, fulfilling God's command and continuing the theme of pilgrimage toward the promised land in redemptive history.

questions.question: What combined theological insight is gained by comparing Genesis 31:30 and Genesis 31:31 regarding the tension between fear and faith in human decisions?
options: Fear always leads to sin without any faith
Fear can motivate actions but is tempered by faith and trust in God's protection
Human decisions are irrelevant to God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: Fear can motivate actions but is tempered by faith and trust in God's protection
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:30 shows Laban accusing Jacob of theft due to fear, and Genesis 31:31 reveals Jacob acted out of fear of losing his wives, illustrating human fear influencing decisions even within God's providential plan.

questions.question: How does Genesis 31:49's naming of Mizpah reflect a theological principle about God's role in human relationships and separation?
options: God is indifferent when people are apart
God watches over and guards relationships even in absence
questions.correctAnswer: God watches over and guards relationships even in absence
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:49 states the LORD watches between Jacob and Laban when they are absent from one another, emphasizing God's protective and sustaining role in human relationships across distances.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by Jacob's declaration in Genesis 31:38-39 about his honesty and suffering during his twenty years of service to Laban?
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and perseverance
questions.explanation: In Genesis 31:38-39, Jacob testifies to his integrity and endurance through hardship, illustrating the doctrine of sanctification through faithful perseverance in trials.

questions.question: What does the setting up of the stone pillar and heap of stones signify about the nature of oaths and divine witness in Genesis 31:45-47?
options: Oaths are meaningless without human witnesses
Oaths involve tangible signs and invoke God's presence as witness
Stone markers are purely cultural with no spiritual significance
Divine witness is unnecessary for agreements
questions.correctAnswer: Oaths involve tangible signs and invoke God's presence as witness
questions.explanation: Genesis 31:45-47 describes Jacob and Laban setting up stones as physical witnesses and naming the site, affirming the seriousness of oaths with divine presence as ultimate witness.
